blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten the function: skip rows with an empty email with an early `continue` (and say why such rows are dropped); resolve the account id first (existing or newly created) and then run a single seat loop, extracted into a helper such as `add_missing_seats(db, account_id, existing_seats, &row.seats)`, instead of the two copies of the `seat.contains('@')` / `add_seat` / `created += 1` block (lines 21-24 and 32-35). Name the unexplained filters: replace `seat.contains('@')` by a named predicate (e.g. `is_seat_email`) with a comment on why seats without `@` are silently ignored, and comment why seats are only added to an existing account when its plan differs from the row's (`account.plan != row.plan`) — a newcomer reading line 18 cannot tell whether that condition is a business rule or an inverted test, and would likely misread that an existing account on the same plan never gets its new seats. The doc comment should also say that existing accounts' plans are not updated and which rows are skipped.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep and hides its rules in unexplained conditions
